name: ChainSwap MappingToken receive() unauthorised signatories

classification.summary: The bridge's receive(fromChainId,to,nonce,volume,Signature[]) counted the supplied signature entries towards its threshold without checking that each signatory was an authorised bridge signer, so anyone could mint bridged tokens to themselves.

loss.notes: Migrated from legacy lossUsd/lossOther. The legacy corpus did not consistently distinguish gross from net loss or record valuation provenance.

sources.note: onchain review: proxy 0x089165ac9a7Bf61833Da86268F34A01652543466 created 2021-05-14T06:19:27Z by 0x6132d220feec1f83a9f0718a8bfd296a0ed67619, unrelated to attack sender 0xeda5066780de29d00dfb54581a707ef6f52d8113. It is a ChainSwap InitializableProductProxy: its EIP-1967 implementation slot is zero and it resolves code through IProxyFactory(factory).productImplementations(name), with factory 0xbf515ff38d55737c56d62e8b6a8eea322ec38aa5 (FACTORY_SLOT 0x7a45a402e4cb6e08ebc196f20f66d5d30e67285a2a8aa80503fa409e727a4af1) and name 'MappingToken' (NAME_SLOT 0x4cd9b827ca535ceb0880425d70eff88561ecdf04dc32fcf7ff3b15c587f8a870), so no EIP-1967 Upgraded event is ever emitted. Binary-searching eth_call of productImplementations('MappingToken') over [7395576, 9042275] gives 0x860da66ce2962233112d5f738bec5f14d865e690 at creation and 0xe92998f47118335ba33d1eba87282584f53519b5 from block 8935896 (2021-07-07T02:36:25Z) onwards, unchanged through the incident block (spot-checked at 8950000, 8990000, 9020000, 9042274 and 9042275; it moves again to 0x9c88ffe3779204154e33e4812a5a6507f37b6fea by block 9100000). The 2021-07-07 install is the fix deployed after the 2021-07-02 ChainSwap incident, so the code the attacker hit was three days old. Loss figure $4.4M from the ChainSec DeFi exploit timeline for the 10 July 2021 ChainSwap incident.
